title: Webhook

url.description: URL that webhook requests are sent to

secret.description: Secret included with webhook requests for authentication (sent as HTTP basic auth password with username 'telerivet')

events.description: Array of event types that trigger this webhook. Possible values: `send_status` (message status updates), `send_broadcast` (broadcast sent), `contact_update` (contact added/updated/deleted), `message_metadata` (message metadata updated)

vars.description:
Custom variables stored for this webhook. Variable names may be up to 32 characters in length and can contain the characters a-z, A-Z, 0-9, and _.
 Values may be strings, numbers, or boolean (true/false).
 String values may be up to 4096 bytes in length when encoded as UTF-8.
 Up to 100 variables are supported per object.
 Setting a variable to null will delete the variable.

project_id.description: ID of the project this webhook belongs to

description:
Represents a webhook that is triggered when specific events occur within a project.

 Webhooks allow your server to receive HTTP POST requests when certain events happen, such as when a message's status changes or when a contact is updated.

 When an event occurs that matches a webhook's event types, Telerivet will send an HTTP POST request to the webhook URL with information about the event. For more information about the webhook request format, see the [Webhook API](https://telerivet.com/api/webhook) documentation.

 Note: The Webhook object is not used for notifying your server when incoming messages are received. To notify a URL when incoming messages are received, you can configure a webhook by creating a Service with type incoming_message_webhook.
